related_questions.question: What prevents you from donating plasma?

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors can prevent someone from donating plasma, including certain medical conditions, medications, recent procedures, and risky behaviors. These can be either temporary or permanent, and are in place to protect both the donor and the recipient.
snippet_highlighted_words: certain medical conditions, medications, recent procedures, and risky behaviors

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: Active infections like HIV, Hepatitis B or C, syphilis, or gonorrhea will disqualify you from donating, according to CSL Plasma.

list.title: Transplants:
list.snippet: Organ or bone marrow transplants can lead to deferrals, says Plasma Heroes.

list.title: Chronic Illnesses:
list.snippet: Conditions like heart, lung, liver, or kidney problems can also be a barrier to donation.

list.title: Other:
list.snippet: Some other conditions that may disqualify you include primary immunodeficiency, certain types of cancer, and babesiosis or Chagas disease, according to WebMD and Merck Manuals.
Antibiotics: You may be temporarily deferred while taking antibiotics for an infection.
Blood Thinners: Certain blood thinners require a waiting period after the last dose.
Other Medications: Many other medications, including those for rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, and prostate issues, can lead to deferrals.

list.title: Tattoos and Piercings:
list.snippet: Fresh tattoos and piercings require a waiting period (usually 3-6 months) before donation, says Plasma Heroes.

list.title: Recent Blood Transfusion or Exposure:
list.snippet: You may be deferred after receiving a blood transfusion or coming into contact with someone else's blood, according to PlasmaLab.

list.title: Incarceration:
list.snippet: Spending more than 72 hours in jail or prison can lead to a deferral, notes Plasma Heroes.

list.title: Drug Use:
list.snippet: Injecting drugs or steroids not prescribed by a doctor, or engaging in sex for money or drugs, can make you ineligible.

list.title: Pregnancy:
list.snippet: Pregnancy and a recent abortion or miscarriage can also cause a temporary deferral, says New York Blood Center.
Weight: A minimum weight (usually around 110 lbs) is required.
Age: Some donation centers have age restrictions, often requiring parental consent for younger donors (e.g., 16 or 17 years old).
Recent Travel: Travel to certain areas with high risk of infectious diseases may lead to a deferral, notes Octapharma Plasma.

text_blocks.snippet: It's always best to check with the specific donation center for their complete list of eligibility requirements, as they may vary slightly.
